lesson_title: The Crab That Left Its Shell
hook_text: This crab shell is perfect, but there is no crab inside. Where did it go?
clip_script: Lambert's Bay harbour. Crayfish, mussels, a sea urchin. And in a rock pool, an empty crab shell. No crab. Because a crab wears its skeleton on the outside, like armour. A hollow, curved shell structure: strong, light and protective. But armour cannot grow. So the crab splits it open, climbs out, swells up and grows a new, bigger shell. The old one is left behind. Squeeze an egg evenly in your hand: curves make shells strong!
visual_style: Whiteboard crab climbing out of its old shell, leaving an outline behind, then a hand squeezing an egg.
mood: Mysterious and then surprising, like solving a little puzzle.
pacing: Mystery shell, outer skeleton explained, moult animation, egg test to finish.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and find three shell structures in your kitchen.
